## captain_marvel

Blast-radius containment for cross-reality propagation. An incident gets an explicit propagation budget: the destinations it may reach, and how many hops and effects it may spend. Evaluating a step can only consume that budget; it never adds a destination and never grants authority. A verdict is a plain value. In Koschei, authority only travels as capability tokens.

Decisions and reasons match the Python guardian `koschei/captain_marvel_blast_radius_v1.py`. Digests use the domain-separated `secure.digest` encoding, so they differ from the Python byte layout.

### struct `BlastRadiusBudget`

```ks
origin_reality: String
allowed_destinations: List<String>
max_hops: Int
max_effects: Int
budget_digest: String
```

### struct `PropagationVerdict`

```ks
allowed: Bool
reason: String
remaining_hops: Int
remaining_effects: Int
verdict_digest: String
```

### `captain_marvel.issue_budget`

```ks
fn issue_budget(origin_reality: String, allowed_destinations: List<String>, max_hops: Int, max_effects: Int) -> Result<BlastRadiusBudget, Error>
```

### `captain_marvel.is_canonical_budget`

```ks
fn is_canonical_budget(budget: BlastRadiusBudget) -> Bool
```

True when `budget` is exactly what `issue_budget` returns for its fields: valid limits, canonical destinations and a matching digest. A digest is not a signature; this detects edited or hand-built budgets, not who issued them.

### `captain_marvel.evaluate`

```ks
fn evaluate(budget: BlastRadiusBudget, destination: String, hops_used: Int, effects_used: Int) -> Result<PropagationVerdict, Error>
```

## hela

Irreversible authority death. A tombstone records that a principal's authority was revoked at an epoch. From that epoch on, the authority stays dead: replay, a stale epoch, another reality or a forked state cannot bring it back.

Decisions match the Python guardian `koschei/hela_authority_death_v1.py` for canonical tombstones. Digest inputs are `secure` digests ("sha3-256:" + 64 hex) rather than raw 32-byte values, and the tombstone digest uses the domain-separated `secure.digest` encoding, so it differs from the Python byte layout.

### struct `AuthorityTombstone`

```ks
principal_digest: String
authority_id: String
death_epoch: Int
reality_digest: String
cause_digest: String
previous_tombstone: String
tombstone_digest: String
```

### `hela.bury`

```ks
fn bury(principal_digest: String, authority_id: String, death_epoch: Int, reality_digest: String, cause_digest: String, previous_tombstone: String) -> Result<AuthorityTombstone, Error>
```

### `hela.is_canonical`

```ks
fn is_canonical(tombstone: AuthorityTombstone) -> Bool
```

True when `tombstone` is exactly what `bury` returns for its fields. A digest is not a signature; this detects edited or hand-built tombstones, not who buried the authority.

### `hela.remains_dead`

```ks
fn remains_dead(tombstone: AuthorityTombstone, principal_digest: String, authority_id: String, candidate_epoch: Int) -> Bool
```

True when the candidate authority is still dead. Fails closed: a malformed principal digest or a tombstone that is not canonical counts as dead.

### `hela.is_resurrection_attempt`

```ks
fn is_resurrection_attempt(tombstone: AuthorityTombstone, principal_digest: String, authority_id: String, candidate_epoch: Int) -> Bool
```

The same decision, named for the caller that is about to grant authority.

## list

Written in Koschei. Every function is total and never mutates its input: a result list is always a fresh value. Index arguments outside the valid range produce an Error value; they are never clamped silently.

### `list.is_empty`

```ks
fn is_empty<T>(items: List<T>) -> Bool
```

### `list.first`

```ks
fn first<T>(items: List<T>) -> Option<T>
```

### `list.last`

```ks
fn last<T>(items: List<T>) -> Option<T>
```

### `list.concat`

```ks
fn concat<T>(left: List<T>, right: List<T>) -> List<T>
```

### `list.reverse`

```ks
fn reverse<T>(items: List<T>) -> List<T>
```

### `list.drop`

```ks
fn drop<T>(items: List<T>, count: Int) -> List<T>
```

Drops the first `count` items. A non-positive count keeps every item and a count beyond the length yields an empty list, mirroring List.take.

### `list.slice`

```ks
fn slice<T>(items: List<T>, start: Int, end: Int) -> Result<List<T>, Error>
```

Items from `start` up to but excluding `end`; requires 0 <= start <= end <= length.

### `list.insert_at`

```ks
fn insert_at<T>(items: List<T>, index: Int, item: T) -> Result<List<T>, Error>
```

Inserts `item` before position `index`; requires 0 <= index <= length.

### `list.remove_at`

```ks
fn remove_at<T>(items: List<T>, index: Int) -> Result<List<T>, Error>
```

Removes the item at `index`; requires 0 <= index < length.

### `list.replace_at`

```ks
fn replace_at<T>(items: List<T>, index: Int, item: T) -> Result<List<T>, Error>
```

Replaces the item at `index`; requires 0 <= index < length.

## matrix_horizon

Matrix/Hara pure horizon policy, not the durable SQLite event-horizon fence. This module ports the deterministic cross-Matrix transition requirements: unchanged Veyra/Aevra, different Matrix/Hara and exactly the next epoch. A head digest is an integrity checksum, NOT a signature or proof of which Hara is currently authorized. The caller must use the independently authenticated durable Python fence for atomic tombstones and anti-replay. It creates no authority, performs no I/O and never changes durable state.

### struct `MatrixHorizonProposal`

A *proposed* Matrix horizon, not the durable current record. All digest fields use Koschei domain-separated SHA3-256 text digests; the Python reference's SHA-256 byte encoding is deliberately different.

```ks
veyra_digest: String
aevra_digest: String
matrix_digest: String
hara_digest: String
epoch: Int
previous_hara_digest: String
cause_digest: String
record_digest: String
```

### `matrix_horizon.record`

```ks
fn record(veyra_digest: String, aevra_digest: String, matrix_digest: String, hara_digest: String, epoch: Int, previous_hara_digest: String, cause_digest: String) -> Result<MatrixHorizonProposal, Error>
```

Public because v1 has no private functions. A record that can be constructed is only a self-consistent *claim*. It cannot admit execution.

### `matrix_horizon.genesis`

```ks
fn genesis(veyra_digest: String, aevra_digest: String, matrix_digest: String, hara_digest: String, epoch: Int, cause_digest: String) -> Result<MatrixHorizonProposal, Error>
```

Construct a genesis *proposal*. An external durable fence still has to initialize the current Hara atomically and reject duplicate initialization.

### `matrix_horizon.is_canonical`

```ks
fn is_canonical(head: MatrixHorizonProposal) -> Bool
```

Recompute the complete proposal's content digest. Not an issuer signature; a caller can construct a new consistent proposal without authorization.

### `matrix_horizon.propose_transition`

```ks
fn propose_transition(current: MatrixHorizonProposal, next_veyra_digest: String, next_aevra_digest: String, next_matrix_digest: String, next_hara_digest: String, next_epoch: Int, cause_digest: String) -> Result<MatrixHorizonProposal, Error>
```

Pure preparation gate reflecting DurableMatrixHorizonFence.advance's identity and next-epoch checks; it does NOT update SQLite, tombstone old Haras, fence stale writers, or prove the supplied head is current. The caller MUST independently authenticate the current durable head.

### `matrix_horizon.matches_snapshot`

```ks
fn matches_snapshot(head: MatrixHorizonProposal, veyra_digest: String, aevra_digest: String, matrix_digest: String, hara_digest: String, epoch: Int) -> Bool
```

Compare a proposal with a CALLER-SUPPLIED observation; this is not require_current(), because only the durable fence knows current state.

## morag

An abandoned artifact expires. Every admitted artifact has a support window: who maintains it and until which day. After the window ends it is not admitted unless a named maintainer has published a dated backport statement for exactly that artifact. Without a known window it is not admitted at all: unknown support is treated as no support.

Identities are content digests ("sha3-256:" + hex), never version labels, so a backported build is a different identity with its own window. Days count from 1970-01-01 (UTC) and are supplied by the caller: a decision is the same wherever and whenever it is replayed.

The PHP2Shell figures behind this planet: 23 million of the 41.9 million version-disclosing PHP services ran on branches that no longer receive fixes.

### struct `SupportWindow`

```ks
identity: String
maintainer: String
until_day: Int
```

### struct `MaintainerBackport`

```ks
identity: String
maintainer: String
until_day: Int
```

### struct `SupportVerdict`

```ks
admitted: Bool
reason: String
maintainer: String
until_day: Int
verdict_digest: String
```

### `morag.verdict`

```ks
fn verdict(admitted: Bool, reason: String, identity: String, today: Int, maintainer: String, until_day: Int) -> Result<SupportVerdict, Error>
```

Builds the verdict of `check`; public only because Koschei v1 has no private functions.

### `morag.check`

```ks
fn check(identity: String, today: Int, windows: List<SupportWindow>, backports: List<MaintainerBackport>) -> Result<SupportVerdict, Error>
```

## secure

Written in Koschei over the kernel `sha3_256` digest, which delegates to an audited host implementation: Koschei implements no cryptographic primitive. Digests are self-describing ("sha3-256:" + 64 lowercase hex characters), so a later algorithm can live beside this one without ambiguity.

### `secure.hash`

```ks
fn hash(value: String) -> Result<String, Error>
```

### `secure.hash_bytes`

```ks
fn hash_bytes(value: Bytes) -> Result<String, Error>
```

The digest of raw bytes, in the same self-describing form as `hash`. For a String, `hash(text)` and `hash_bytes(text.to_bytes())` are the same digest.

### `secure.digest`

```ks
fn digest(context: String, parts: List<String>) -> Result<String, Error>
```

Domain-separated digest of a context label and an ordered list of parts. Every field is written as "<length>:<text>", with lengths in characters, so two different (context, parts) inputs can never encode to the same bytes. The context names the purpose (for example "koschei.marvel.hela.tombstone/v1") and may not be empty: an unlabelled digest could be replayed in another purpose.

### `secure.zero_digest`

```ks
fn zero_digest() -> String
```

The all-zero digest: the conventional "no previous record" link at the start of a chain. No known input hashes to it.

### `secure.is_digest`

```ks
fn is_digest(value: String) -> Bool
```

True when `value` has the shape this module produces.

## strange

Bounded look-ahead over a declared path of authority transitions. Before any effect runs, `simulate` predicts whether the path would cross a forbidden effect, break the authority timeline or widen authority. It performs no effect and grants no authority: it only reads the steps it is given.

Decisions, the index of the first violation and the reasons match the Python guardian `koschei/strange_future_paths_v1.py`. Authority sets are lists compared as sets. The path digest uses the domain-separated `secure.digest` encoding, so it differs from the Python byte layout.

### struct `FutureStep`

```ks
effect: String
target: String
authority_before: List<String>
authority_after: List<String>
```

### struct `FutureVerdict`

```ks
safe: Bool
first_violation: Option<Int>
reason: String
path_digest: String
```

### `strange.verdict`

```ks
fn verdict(safe: Bool, first_violation: Option<Int>, reason: String, parts: List<String>) -> Result<FutureVerdict, Error>
```

Builds the verdict of `simulate`; public only because Koschei v1 has no private functions.

### `strange.simulate`

```ks
fn simulate(steps: List<FutureStep>, max_steps: Int, forbidden_effects: List<String>) -> Result<FutureVerdict, Error>
```

## text

Written in Koschei on top of the String kernel (length, contains, trim, split, join). A search pattern that must locate something (separator, needle, old text) may not be empty: an empty pattern has no single meaning, so it produces None or an Error value instead of a guessed answer.

### `text.is_empty`

```ks
fn is_empty(value: String) -> Bool
```

### `text.is_blank`

```ks
fn is_blank(value: String) -> Bool
```

### `text.starts_with`

```ks
fn starts_with(value: String, prefix: String) -> Bool
```

Prefix and suffix tests compare UTF-8 bytes: a valid UTF-8 text starts (or ends) with another exactly when its bytes do, and a byte slice never needs more than the value itself, so any String within the value budget works.

### `text.ends_with`

```ks
fn ends_with(value: String, suffix: String) -> Bool
```

### `text.strip_prefix`

```ks
fn strip_prefix(value: String, prefix: String) -> Option<String>
```

### `text.strip_suffix`

```ks
fn strip_suffix(value: String, suffix: String) -> Option<String>
```

Returns the text before a trailing `suffix`, or None when the value does not end with it.

### `text.before`

```ks
fn before(value: String, separator: String) -> Option<String>
```

Text before the first occurrence of `separator`. None also when the value holds more pieces than one List may (KS3502): the answer is not computed.

### `text.after`

```ks
fn after(value: String, separator: String) -> Option<String>
```

Text after the first occurrence of `separator`; None as for `before`.

### `text.count`

```ks
fn count(value: String, needle: String) -> Result<Int, Error>
```

Number of non-overlapping occurrences, counted left to right.

### `text.replace`

```ks
fn replace(value: String, old: String, replacement: String) -> Result<String, Error>
```

Replaces every non-overlapping occurrence, left to right.

### `text.lines`

```ks
fn lines(value: String) -> Result<List<String>, Error>
```

Lines separated by "\n". One trailing "\r" is removed from each line, and a final "\n" does not start an extra empty line. A value with more lines than one List may hold is an Err (KS3502), never a shortened list.

### `text.words`

```ks
fn words(value: String) -> Result<List<String>, Error>
```

Non-empty pieces separated by spaces, tabs, carriage returns or newlines. More pieces than one List may hold is an Err (KS3502), never a shortened list.

### `text.unique_sorted`

```ks
fn unique_sorted(values: List<String>) -> List<String>
```

The distinct values in ascending character order: a canonical set of names. Insertion keeps the work quadratic, which suits the small name sets the library's guardians use.

## wanda

Tamper-evident reality commitments. A reality may evolve epoch by epoch, but a past that was already admitted cannot be silently rewritten: each commitment links to the one before it, and two different commitments for the same reality and epoch are a fork.

Decisions match the Python guardian `koschei/wanda_reality_integrity_v1.py` for canonical commitments. Digest inputs are `secure` digests, and the commitment digest uses the domain-separated `secure.digest` encoding, so it differs from the Python byte layout. A commitment that is not canonical gets the fail-closed answer from every check.

### struct `RealityCommitment`

```ks
reality_id: String
epoch: Int
state_digest: String
authority_digest: String
previous_commitment: String
commitment_digest: String
```

### `wanda.commit`

```ks
fn commit(reality_id: String, epoch: Int, state_digest: String, authority_digest: String, previous_commitment: String) -> Result<RealityCommitment, Error>
```

### `wanda.is_canonical`

```ks
fn is_canonical(commitment: RealityCommitment) -> Bool
```

True when `commitment` is exactly what `commit` returns for its fields. A digest is not a signature; this detects edited or hand-built commitments, not who committed them.

### `wanda.extends`

```ks
fn extends(parent: RealityCommitment, child: RealityCommitment) -> Bool
```

True when `child` is the next epoch of `parent` and links to it.

### `wanda.detects_fork`

```ks
fn detects_fork(first: RealityCommitment, second: RealityCommitment) -> Bool
```

True when two different commitments claim the same reality and epoch. Fails closed: a commitment that is not canonical counts as a fork.

### `wanda.detects_rollback`

```ks
fn detects_rollback(current: RealityCommitment, candidate: RealityCommitment) -> Bool
```

True when `candidate` would move `current` back to the same or an earlier epoch. Fails closed: a commitment that is not canonical counts as a rollback.

## xandar

Nova Corps keeps the record: a known-vulnerable artifact is not admitted. An advisory names what it affects by content digest ("sha3-256:" + hex), never by version label. A label can claim a fix that is not there, or hide a fix a distribution backported without changing it; a digest cannot.

An advisory is evidence. It can only refuse admission, never grant it, and a feed whose meaning is uncertain refuses everything: an advisory without an id, a duplicate id, or an affected entry that is not a digest makes the whole feed malformed. Every verdict carries the digest of the exact feed it was decided against.

Xandar alone is not a defense: PHP2Shell was exploited before its advisory existed. Capability confinement, which needs no advisory, stays first.

### struct `SecurityAdvisory`

```ks
id: String
affected: List<String>
```

### struct `AdvisoryVerdict`

```ks
admitted: Bool
reason: String
advisories: List<String>
feed_digest: String
verdict_digest: String
```

### `xandar.feed_digest`

```ks
fn feed_digest(advisories: List<SecurityAdvisory>) -> Result<String, Error>
```

Digest of a feed in canonical form: advisories by ascending id, each with its distinct affected digests in ascending order. Input order never changes the digest.

### `xandar.is_well_formed`

```ks
fn is_well_formed(advisories: List<SecurityAdvisory>) -> Bool
```

True when every advisory has an id, ids are distinct, and every advisory names at least one affected digest.

### `xandar.verdict`

```ks
fn verdict(admitted: Bool, reason: String, matched: List<String>, identity: String, feed: String) -> Result<AdvisoryVerdict, Error>
```

Builds the verdict of `check`; public only because Koschei v1 has no private functions.

### `xandar.check`

```ks
fn check(identity: String, advisories: List<SecurityAdvisory>) -> Result<AdvisoryVerdict, Error>
```
